purpose: The ways a running java program can HOLD layer-1 content. Not layer 1 (the data is fixed), not layer 3 (no operations beyond load-and-read-back), not the type system.
reference: language knowledge, checked against ../type_vocabulary/raw/java.types.json as a candidate checklist only (superseded node; not a decision instrument).

nothing.note: the one hole every reference kind shares; a co-node value with no runtime marker of its own.
absence spelled as a case of a two-case shape, with a declared element kind and no null inside it.
a reference kind whose only reachable value is the null hole itself.

truth.note: primitive two-value holder, no null hole reachable.
boxed co-node of boolean; a reference kind, so it can also carry the null hole.

whole.note: narrow fixed-width holder, sixteen bits signed; the edge values do not fit.
sixty-four-bit signed holder, the usual whole-number workhorse.
boxed co-node of int; a reference kind that can also carry the null hole.
arbitrary precision whole number built from decimal text, unbounded above and below.

fractional.note: IEEE double, the default fractional holder.
IEEE single; holds every base value at lower precision, and silently rounds the wide whole edges.
arbitrary precision decimal built from digit text, with no concept of the special non-numbers at all.

text.note: immutable utf-16 text, the ordinary holder.
text unpacked into a mutable run of utf-16 units; the clef needs two units for one codepoint here.
a mutable text buffer built over the same utf-16 unit run.
holds text only as encoded bytes; the codepoints are gone until decoded back.

sequence.note: a fixed-length array of references; each slot may hold a different kind, so it takes the mixed row.

probes.mixed: Object[] v = new Object[]{1L, "two", 3.0, true, null};

sequence.note: a fixed-length array of primitive longs, one declared element kind, no null hole reachable in any slot.

probes.mixed: long[] v = new long[]{1L, "two", 3.0, true, null};

sequence.note: growable ordered run backed by an array, one declared element kind.

probes.mixed: ArrayList<Object> v = new ArrayList<>(); v.add(1L); v.add("two"); v.add(3.0); v.add(true); v.add(null);

sequence.note: an immutable ordered run built at construction time; this shape refuses the null hole in any slot.
ordered run built of linked nodes rather than a backing array.

probes.mixed: LinkedList<Object> v = new LinkedList<>(); v.add(1L); v.add("two"); v.add(3.0); v.add(true); v.add(null);

sequence.note: ordered run open at both ends, backed by a resizable array; refuses the null hole outright.

probes.mixed: ArrayDeque<Object> v = new ArrayDeque<>(); v.add(1L); v.add("two"); v.add(3.0); v.add(true); v.add(null);

keyed.note: name to element, no order kept between runs.

probes.flat: HashMap<String, Long> v = new HashMap<>(); v.put("a", 1L); v.put("b", 2L); v.put("c", 3L);
probes.intlike: HashMap<String, Object> v = new HashMap<>(); v.put("1", "string-one-key"); v.put("b", 2L);
probes.emptykey: HashMap<String, String> v = new HashMap<>(); v.put("", "empty-string key");
probes.nested: HashMap<String, Object> inner = new HashMap<>(); inner.put("inner", java.util.List.of(1L, 2L)); HashMap<String, Object> v = new HashMap<>(); v.put("outer", inner);

keyed.note: the same name-to-element grouping, but insertion order is kept when reading it back.

probes.flat: LinkedHashMap<String, Long> v = new LinkedHashMap<>(); v.put("a", 1L); v.put("b", 2L); v.put("c", 3L);
probes.intlike: LinkedHashMap<String, Object> v = new LinkedHashMap<>(); v.put("1", "string-one-key"); v.put("b", 2L);
probes.emptykey: LinkedHashMap<String, String> v = new LinkedHashMap<>(); v.put("", "empty-string key");
probes.nested: LinkedHashMap<String, Object> inner = new LinkedHashMap<>(); inner.put("inner", java.util.List.of(1L, 2L)); LinkedHashMap<String, Object> v = new LinkedHashMap<>(); v.put("outer", inner);

keyed.note: the same grouping held in sorted key order at all times.

probes.flat: TreeMap<String, Long> v = new TreeMap<>(); v.put("a", 1L); v.put("b", 2L); v.put("c", 3L);
probes.intlike: TreeMap<String, Object> v = new TreeMap<>(); v.put("1", "string-one-key"); v.put("b", 2L);
probes.emptykey: TreeMap<String, String> v = new TreeMap<>(); v.put("", "empty-string key");
probes.nested: TreeMap<String, Object> inner = new TreeMap<>(); inner.put("inner", java.util.List.of(1L, 2L)); TreeMap<String, Object> v = new TreeMap<>(); v.put("outer", inner);

keyed.spelling: record R(long a, long b, long c) {}
keyed.note: names fixed when the shape is written, not when the data arrives; the odd keys are not spellable as field names.

probes.empty: record R0() {} R0 v = new R0();
probes.flat: record R3(long a, long b, long c) {} R3 v = new R3(1, 2, 3);
probes.intlike: record RI(String f1, String b) {} RI v = new RI("string-one-key", "2");
probes.emptykey: record RE(String field) {} RE v = new RE("empty-string key");
probes.nested: record RN(java.util.List<Long> outer) {} RN v = new RN(java.util.List.of(1L, 2L));

keyed.spelling: class C { long a, b, c; }
keyed.note: names fixed when the shape is written; the int-like key and the empty key are not spellable as java field names.

probes.empty: class C0 { public String toString() { return "{}"; } } C0 v = new C0();
probes.flat: class C3 { long a, b, c; C3(long a, long b, long c) { this.a=a; this.b=b; this.c=c; } public String toString() { return "{a=" + a + ", b=" + b + ", c=" + c + "}"; } } C3 v = new C3(1, 2, 3);
probes.intlike: class CI { String 1; String b; CI(String x, String y) { this.1=x; this.b=y; } public String toString() { return "{1=" + 1 + ", b=" + b + "}"; } } CI v = new CI("string-one-key", "2");
probes.emptykey: class CE { String ; CE(String x) { this.=x; } public String toString() { return "{=" +  + "}"; } } CE v = new CE("empty-string key");
probes.nested: class CN { java.util.List<Long> outer; CN(java.util.List<Long> outer) { this.outer=outer; } public String toString() { return "{outer=" + outer + "}"; } } CN v = new CN(java.util.List.of(1L, 2L));

nesting.note: nesting by repeating the same holder kind; every level takes the same declared element kind.

probes.seq_in_map: java.util.Map<String, Object> v = java.util.Map.of("outer", java.util.Map.of("inner", List.of(1L, 2L)));
probes.mixed_depth: List<Object> v = List.of(1L, List.of(2L, java.util.Map.of("k", "t")), true, java.util.Collections.singletonList(null));

nesting.note: keyed grouping used as the co-node at every nesting level, each level typed as Object to hold the level below.

probes.seq_in_seq: Map<String, Object> inner = Map.of("0", List.of(1L, 2L), "1", List.of(3L, 4L)); Map<String, Object> v = inner;
probes.seq_in_map: Map<String, Object> v = Map.of("outer", Map.of("inner", List.of(1L, 2L)));
probes.mixed_depth: Map<String, Object> v = Map.of("a", 1L, "b", List.of(2L, Map.of("k", "t")), "c", true);

nesting.note: an array of arrays; each row is itself a reference-holding array so rows can differ in length and kind.

probes.seq_in_map: Object[] inner = new Object[]{"inner", new Object[]{1L, 2L}}; Object[] v = new Object[]{"outer", inner};
probes.mixed_depth: Object[] v = new Object[]{1L, new Object[]{2L, new Object[]{"k", "t"}}, true, null};

identity.note: an array slot holds a reference, not a copy of what it points to, so two slots can name one node.
a fixed-shape holder whose one field stores a reference, so two holders built from the same field value name one co-node.

identity.spelling: record R(long a, long b, long c) {}
identity.note: a fixed-shape holder of primitive fields; building a second holder from the first's field values copies the numbers, no node is shared.
a fixed-length primitive array; copying its slots into another array copies the numbers themselves, so nothing downstream is shared.
